posts.name: riff.freelance
posts.cooked:
I'll freely admit I wasn't too pleased with Vengence, I mostly bought it for the heroes and then tried the style. I'm still not really sold on Venence style gameplay, but I'm trying to keep an open mind. I'm certain a great deal of how I feel about this is my playgroup (or lack thereof) as I play Sentinels in the flesh much less often than I want and so many of my friends are still easing into how the basics work. I'm not quite ready to spring Vengence on them. I almost didn't buy Villians (missed the preorder campaign, but did in fact preorder it. Got my first preorder promos here.) 

 

I guess you could put this in the unreasonable request thread, but I wish every Villian had a standard and Venence style deck because some of the Vengence ones are just so nifty. Vengence isn't all that hard to play, but it is daunting. My 2 cents.

All that being said I kinda fear change. I like my games to flow in a way I can "officiate" with some authority. As it stands everyone is looking to me to make things run smooth, I would hate to dissapoint. For that matter I think I've played against Warfang all of once. She looks great, but I need to make certain I can keep the game super smooth for the players I'm likely to have on hand. They're not simpletons by any means, but they just really don't feel a desire to spend time learning "how to play" a game when that time could be used on having fun. I really don't understand these guys at all. They play D&D, video games like Diablo, Airsoft and other group hobbies, but don't want to spend any downtime on the hobby. I upgrade a lot of thier airsoft gear for them, they ask me how to make a character that is good at X in an RPG and I give them options, and they don't ever bother to even look up potential builds for anything. They're cool people but their "geek" is greek to me.

I can't wait for more details about the playstyle comes out. I want to know more about the mission deck (decks?) and how environments interact. I've always thought there would be a way to play with 2 environments, Time Cataclysm and it's keywords just made it seem so obvious.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
Sounds to me like they've got used to being babied a bit. Maybe a little tough love is in order?

I know a group of friends where basically everything they do is organised by one couple. Gaming sessions are at their house, they feed everyone, they buy all the games, they decide what will be played, they teach the games, they organise the gaming vacation week they do every year. And everyone else in the group does exactly nothing but passively enjoy the advantages of that couple's work.

That's fine if everyone's happy with it, but it's often very stressful on the person who's taking the "parental" role. I mean helping someone out is one thing, but doing everything for them is another - of course they don't want to learn to do hard things for themselves because it's easier if someone else does it.

Me? I'd make it clear that I'm happy to help, but they have to work too and take responsibility for their own stuff. They are missing out on a lot of the fun!
